\section[protestar]{protestar — to protest; to complain}

\label{lesson:ES-C604-protestar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the justice, then the Spanish for unfair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: protestar}
\textbf{protestar} — \textquotedblleft{}to protest; to complain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los vecinos protestan por el ruido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The neighbours are protesting about the noise.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Protestar por} or \emph{contra} something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{protestar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{protestari} 'to declare publicly', built on \emph{testis} 'witness' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{protestar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{protestar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{protestar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the justice, then the Spanish for unfair, then say \emph{protestar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does protestar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To protest; to complain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[expresar]{expresar — to express}

\label{lesson:ES-C604-expresar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for unfair, then the Spanish for to protest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: expresar}
\textbf{expresar} — \textquotedblleft{}to express\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Quiero expresar mi opinión.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I want to express my opinion.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Expresarse} — to express yourself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{expresar} is built on \emph{expreso} (EtymDB), a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{expressus} 'pressed out, clear', from \emph{exprimere}, built on \emph{premere} 'to press'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{expresar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{expresar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{expresar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for unfair, then the Spanish for to protest, then say \emph{expresar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does expresar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To express\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[polémico]{polémico — controversial}

\label{lesson:ES-C604-polemico}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to protest, then the Spanish for to express.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: polémico}
\textbf{polémico} — \textquotedblleft{}controversial\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es un tema muy polémico.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is a very controversial subject.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La polémica} — the controversy.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{polémico} is a learned word usually traced to Greek \emph{polemikos} 'warlike', built on \emph{polemos} 'war', probably through French \emph{polémique}; EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polémico}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polémico}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{polémico}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to protest, then the Spanish for to express, then say \emph{polémico} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does polémico mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Controversial\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[reclamar]{reclamar — to claim, to demand; to complain}

\label{lesson:ES-C604-reclamar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to express, then the Spanish for controversial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reclamar}
\textbf{reclamar} — \textquotedblleft{}to claim, to demand; to complain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Reclamo mi dinero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am claiming my money back.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Reclamar a la empresa} — to complain to the company.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reclamar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{reclamare} 'to cry out against', built on \emph{clamare} 'to shout' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reclamar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reclamar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{reclamar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to express, then the Spanish for controversial, then say \emph{reclamar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does reclamar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To claim, to demand; to complain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[reivindicar]{reivindicar — to demand, to claim (a right)}

\label{lesson:ES-C604-reivindicar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for controversial, then the Spanish for to claim.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reivindicar}
\textbf{reivindicar} — \textquotedblleft{}to demand, to claim (a right)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los trabajadores reivindican mejores sueldos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The workers are demanding better pay.}
\end{quote}

Spelling: \emph{reivindiqué}. \emph{La reivindicación} — the demand.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reivindicar} is a learned word built from Latin \emph{rei}, a form of \emph{res} 'thing, property', and \emph{vindicare} 'to claim' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reivindicar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{reivindicar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for controversial, then the Spanish for to claim, then say \emph{reivindicar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
